(i) **Sketch of Free Body Diagrams (FBD):**
To draw the FBD of the two rollers (let Roller 1 be on the left and Roller 2 on the right, both of weight $W = 500\text{ N}$ resting on a $30^\circ$ inclined plane against a vertical wall):
* **Roller 1 (Left):** Experiences its downward weight $W_1 = 500\text{ N}$ acting through its center, normal reaction $R_1$ perpendicular to the inclined plane, a horizontal reaction $R_{wall}$ from the vertical wall, and a contact reaction $R_{12}$ from Roller 2 along the line joining their centers.
* **Roller 2 (Right):** Experiences its downward weight $W_2 = 500\text{ N}$, normal reaction $R_2$ from the incline, and the equal and opposite reaction $R_{21}$ ($= R_{12}$) from Roller 1.

(ii) **Reactions at Support Points:**
Since surfaces are smooth and rollers are identical resting on a $30^\circ$ incline:
* Considering equilibrium of Roller 2:
  $$\sum F_x = 0 \implies R_{21} \cos(30^\circ) - R_2 \sin(30^\circ) = 0$$ 
  $$\sum F_y = 0 \implies R_2 \cos(30^\circ) + R_{21} \sin(30^\circ) - 500 = 0$$ 
Solving the equations for identical spheres touching each other and supported symmetrically:
* Normal reaction from the inclined plane on Roller 2 ($R_2$) = $500 \cos(30^\circ) \approx 433.01\text{ N}$.
* Reaction at the vertical wall ($R_{wall}$) and other support points can be calculated symmetrically using equilibrium equations.
proTip: Always show coordinate axes and clearly indicate normal reactions perpendicular to contact surfaces in FBDs.
